rows.why: Most of the rows ('0s', '1d0h0m0s0ms') depend on whether zero and zero-valued components are accepted. Item 7's pick accepts them and returns their sum. Item 3 (day unit) also fits the 'd' rows, and its pick agrees too.
Item 5 asks whether whitespace is allowed. The scenario trims spaces and newlines around the input, but the pick rejects spaces without exception, so '  45m\n' would fail.

Most rows (decimal, signs, inner spaces, uppercase unit) fall under item 5's whitespace/sign/fraction/casing question. Its pick rejects all of them. Items 1, 2 and 8 cover the bare number, empty and '3w' rows, and their picks also reject.
No item asks whether a count may be larger than the next unit up (e.g. 90m). Item 4 is about unit order and repeats, not count size.
Item 4 asks about order and repeats. Its pick rejects out-of-order and repeated units, which is what the scenario expects.
Item 6 asks for the maximum. Its pick caps at 9007199254740991 inclusive, so the largest value parses.
Item 6 covers the maximum and overflow. Its pick returns InvalidDuration above the cap and on u64 overflow.
The scenario expects the greedy largest-unit split (5400000 -> '1h30m'). Item 10's pick prints the shortest string, '90m'. Item 9's pick ('0s' for zero) also conflicts with the expected '0ms'.
Item 10 decides which split is printed. For this value the split starting at days is also the shortest, so the pick gives '104249991d8h59m991ms'.
No item asks whether formatting and then parsing must give the original number back.
Item 12 asks how formatting handles values above the maximum. Its pick returns a MillisecondsOutOfRange error for anything above 9007199254740991, u64::MAX included.
